heroData.title: Employer of Record (EOR) in Equatorial Guinea
heroData.subtitle: Compliant global hiring without a local entity
heroData.description: Navigate Equatorial Guinea's specialized labor market, including local content requirements and OHADA-compliant employment frameworks, through our comprehensive EOR solutions.
heroData.bestFor: O&G service providers, tech startups, and NGOs looking to hire in Malabo or Bata.

steps.title: Contract Drafting & Compliance Review
steps.description: Preparation of an employment contract that complies with the 2012 Labor Code (Ley de Trabajo). The contract must specify the professional category, salary in XAF, and must be drafted in Spanish.

steps.title: INSESO & WPF Registration
steps.description: The employee is registered with the National Institute of Social Security (INSESO) and the Work Protection Fund (WPF). This step is mandatory before the first day of work.

steps.title: Medical Clearance & Work Permit
steps.description: Expatriate employees must undergo a medical examination and obtain a 'Certificado Médico' from a local clinic. The EOR then proceeds with the Work Permit application.

steps.title: Local Bank Account & Payroll Initialization
steps.description: Assisting the employee in opening a local bank account (e.g., CCEIBANK, BGFIBank). Salary must be paid into a local account to ensure proper tax withholding (IRPF).

steps.title: Equipment & IT Setup
steps.description: Delivery of hardware (laptops, phones) and setup of local connectivity. The EOR ensures that the employee has stable internet access via GITGE fiber or local ISPs.

rows.label: EOR Management Fee
values: Depends on role complexity and status

items.title: Local Content Quotas
items.text: Under Ministerial Order 2/2020, companies in the hydrocarbon sector must prioritize Equatoguinean citizens. Expatriate hires must be justified.

items.title: New Tax Code 2025 (Law 1/2024)
items.text: The 2025 tax reform caps Personal Income Tax (IRPF) at 25% for high earners, significantly improving net pay for executives.

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Probation periods are typically limited to 3 months for technicians and 6 months for management roles.

steps.title: Periodic Risk Assessment
steps.description: Mandatory workplace risk assessments must be updated every 5 years as per the latest 2025 directives (Occupational Safety and Health Act).

steps.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
steps.description: The EOR ensures all employees in technical or field roles are provided with certified PPE matching international safety standards (ISO/EN).

steps.title: Emergency Protocol Training
steps.description: Conducting Spanish-language safety drills and training sessions for fire hazards, medical emergencies, and regional health risks (e.g., Malaria).

items.title: Connectivity Standards
items.text: Leveraging the GITGE submarine cable network to provide redundant high-speed fiber links for remote roles in Malabo and Bata.

items.title: Cybersecurity protocols
items.text: Implementing mandatory VPN and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to safeguard corporate data accessed from regional IP addresses.

items.title: Home Office Stipends
items.text: Guidance on providing XAF-denominated stipends for energy and backup power (UPS) to ensure continuity during local utility fluctuations.

faqs.question: Can I hire expats using an EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it requires 'Solicitud de Trabajo' approval. The EOR acts as the legal sponsor and manages the work permit process.

faqs.question: What is the typical management fee?
faqs.answer: Fees generally range between $200 and $600 per employee per month, depending on the risk tier and support level.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle health insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes, EOR providers typically offer private supplemental insurance from firms like ASCOMA or ALLIANZ to complement the INSESO state coverage.

steps.title: Variable Data Collection
steps.description: Collection of overtime hours, shift differentials, and bonus approvals. Data must be submitted by the 20th of the month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculations
steps.description: Calculation of base salary, housing allowances, and transport subsidies. Deduction of 4.5% INSESO and sliding scale IRPF.

steps.title: Tax & Social Security Disbursement
steps.description: Payment of withheld IRPF to the Public Treasury and INSESO/WPF contributions by the 15th of the following month.

steps.title: Payslip Distribution
steps.description: Generation of Spanish-language payslips (Nominas). Digital or physical delivery is mandated by labor law.

items.title: Form 104 (IRPF)
items.text: Monthly declaration of personal income tax withheld from employees, due to the General Directorate of Taxes.

items.title: INSESO Nominative List
items.text: Detailed monthly list of employees, their gross salaries, and calculated contributions submitted to the Social Security office.

items.title: Annual Summary (DAS)
items.text: Consolidated annual declaration of all salaries and withholdings paid throughout the fiscal year, filed by end of April.

items.title: Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Delays in INSESO or IRPF payments beyond the 15th trigger automatic 10% penalties. Habitual delays block 'Certificado de Solvencia'.

items.title: XAF Peg & Liquidity
items.text: The XAF is pegged to the Euro (655.957). Local bank liquidity issues can occasionally delay offshore-to-local funding.

items.title: 13th Month Salary
items.text: Customary in O&G and banking. Usually paid in December and subject to standard withholding taxes.

steps.title: BEAC Authorization
steps.description: Processing outward remittances through authorized local banks, ensuring all documentation matches the commercial contracts filed with the Ministry of Commerce.

steps.title: Proof of Tax Payment
steps.description: Verification that all IRPF and WHT have been cleared before funds can be transferred offshore to parent company accounts.

steps.title: Supporting Document Filing
steps.description: Maintaining a 5-year archive of transfer justifications (contracts, invoices, tax receipts) for periodic Central Bank audits.

faqs.question: Can I pay in USD?
faqs.answer: Labor law requires XAF for local compliance. Split-payroll is possible but the local portion must cover all taxes.

faqs.question: What is the IRPF cap in 2025?
faqs.answer: Under Law 1/2024, the highest personal income tax bracket is now capped at 25%.

faqs.question: Is digital payslip delivery allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the employee can access it and the system complies with Law 1/2016 on data protection.

items.title: Employee INSESO
items.text: Fixed at 4.5% of gross salary, deducted at source every month.

items.title: Employee WPF
items.text: Small 0.5% deduction for the labor protection fund contribution.

items.title: Net-to-Gross Ratio
items.text: Typically, net pay is roughly 70-75% of gross for mid-tier salaries in GQ.

steps.title: Gross Base Salary
steps.description: The base amount agreed upon in the employment contract (in XAF).

steps.title: Expatriate Status
steps.description: Selecting yes/no to apply specific housing allowance valuations (typically 20% capped).

steps.title: Family Units
steps.description: Applicable deductions for dependents (Hijos) which slightly reduce the IRPF liability.

faqs.question: Does it include 13th month?
faqs.answer: The calculator allows you to toggle 13th-month accruals for a full annual view.

faqs.question: Are the rates confirmed for 2025?
faqs.answer: Yes, we have integrated the Law 1/2024 tax code updates effective Jan 1, 2025.

faqs.question: Is food allowance taxable?
faqs.answer: Small 'Ticket Restaurant' style stipends have minor exemptions; cash food allowances are fully taxable.

faqs.question: How do I calculate overtime?
faqs.answer: Overtime is calculated based on the 2012 Labor Code: +25% for the first few hours, +50% for subsequent hours, and +100% for Sundays and holidays.

heroData.title: Business Incorporation in Equatorial Guinea
heroData.subtitle: Establish a legal presence in the CEMAC region
heroData.description: Comprehensive support for setting up SARL or SA entities, obtaining Guichet Unique approval, and navigating the 2024 OHADA revisions.
heroData.bestFor: International corporations looking to establish a permanent business unit.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Verification of availability at the 'Registro de la Propiedad y Mercantil' in Malabo.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Minimum share capital (1,000,000 XAF for SARL) must be deposited in a provisional local bank account.

steps.title: Notarization
steps.description: Signing the Articles of Association (Estatutos) before a licensed Notary Public.

steps.title: Guichet Unique
steps.description: One-stop submission for NIF, RCCM, and Labor License at the Single Window for Corporate Formalities.

items.title: SARL
items.text: Limited Liability Company. Best for mid-sized ventures. Minimum capital 1M XAF.

items.title: SA
items.text: Joint Stock Company. Required for large investments. Minimum capital 10M XAF. Needs a Board.

items.title: Branch Conversion
items.text: Foreign branches are limited to 2 years, renewable once. Then conversion to a local subsidiary is mandatory.

steps.title: Tax Clearance Gathering
steps.description: Obtaining 'Certificado de estar al corriente' from both the Tax and Social Security departments.

steps.title: Activity Report Submission
steps.description: Brief annual report to the Ministry of Commerce outlining business progress and local employment stats.

steps.title: Fee Payment
steps.description: Payment of the annual 'Licencia de Actividad' fee, which varies based on the company's size and sector.

items.title: KYC Documentation
items.text: Banks like BGFIBank and CCEI require apostilled Articles of Association and verified IDs of all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs).

items.title: Minimum Balance
items.text: Maintenance of a minimum operating balance in XAF to cover statutory payments (INSESO/Taxes) for at least three months of operations.

items.title: Online Banking Security
items.text: Guidance on setting up tokens and dual-authorization workflows to prevent unauthorized disbursements from the local entity.

faqs.question: Can I have 100% foreign ownership?
faqs.answer: Yes, for most sectors. Hydrocarbons sector requires specific local participation (usually 35%).

faqs.question: What is the Guichet Unique?
faqs.answer: The Single Window for Corporate Formalities, a centralized hub for all administrative registrations in Malabo.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, a registered physical address with a verified lease is mandatory for final licensing.

items.title: SYSCOHADA Compliance
items.text: Mandatory use of the OHADA chart of accounts for all local entities.

items.title: Receipt Validity
items.text: Receipts must be physical originals with the vendor's NIF clearly stated for tax deductibility.

items.title: Audit Thresholds
items.text: Comisario de Cuentas is mandatory if SARL turnover > 250M XAF or > 50 employees.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Intercompany charges for management fees are strictly scrutinized; must be at 'arm's length' with documentation.

items.title: Fixed Asset Depreciation
items.text: Must follow the specific asset life-cycles defined in the 2024 revised OHADA tax guidelines.

items.title: Inventory Valuation
items.text: The FIFO method is generally preferred by local tax authorities to avoid manipulation of the MIT (Minimum Income Tax) base.

items.title: Asset Register
items.text: Maintaining a digital register of all physical assets located in Equatorial Guinea, including purchase date, cost, and serial numbers.

items.title: Depreciation Schedules
items.text: Applying the mandatory OHADA depreciation rates (e.g., 20% for computers, 10% for office furniture) to ensure tax compliance.

items.title: Physical Verification
items.text: Guidance on conducting annual physical audits of inventory and assets to match the 'Bilan' (Balance Sheet) records.

faqs.question: What is the functional currency?
faqs.answer: The Central African Franc (XAF), which has a fixed exchange rate to the Euro.

faqs.question: Can I use QuickBooks?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must map the chart of accounts to the SYSCOHADA numbering for statutory filings.

faqs.question: When is the the deadline for the annual return?
faqs.answer: April 30th of the following fiscal year is the standard deadline for all SA and SARL entities.

faqs.question: What is ANIF?
faqs.answer: The National Agency for Financial Investigation, the primary AML regulator in Equatorial Guinea.

faqs.question: Is anti-corruption law strict?
faqs.answer: Yes, Law 1/2017 prohibits all forms of bribery; enforcement has increased with international oversight.

faqs.question: What happens if a labor audit fails?
faqs.answer: Immediate fines starting at 500,000 XAF and potential suspension of work permits for expat staff.

items.title: CIT Reduction
items.text: The rate is reduced from 35% to 25% under Law 1/2024 to stimulate non-oil investment.

items.title: Minimum Income Tax (MIT)
items.text: A floor of 1.5% of annual turnover applies, regardless of profitability.

items.title: VAT Standard Rate
items.text: 15% applies to most transactions, with 6% for basic goods and 0% for exports.

steps.title: Monthly Filings
steps.description: VAT, IRPF, and WHT returns due by the 15th.

steps.title: CIT Installments
steps.description: Three quarterly payments based on prior year: March, July, November.

steps.title: Annual Final Return
steps.description: Submission of the 'Impuesto sobre Sociedades' by April 30th.

items.title: Exemption Suspension
items.text: The government suspended most tax exemptions for non-oil companies as of Feb 19, 2025, to bolster fiscal revenue.

items.title: Investment Law Benefits
items.text: Historically, sectors like agriculture and tourism could receive 5-10 year holidays, though these are under review.

items.title: CEMAC Treaty
items.text: Reductions on WHT are available if the service provider is resident in another CEMAC state with proper documentation.

faqs.question: Is there a capital gains tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically taxed as ordinary corporate income at the 25% rate.

faqs.question: Can I carry forward losses?
faqs.answer: Yes, for up to 3 years under standard OHADA rules.

faqs.question: What is the 'Licencia Fiscal'?
faqs.answer: The annual business fiscal license required for all commercial entities, renewed every Jan/Feb.
